description: Two ramps that move their outputs up or down over time at a speed a knob and a jack set between them, each held between a low and a high limit

params.text: Sets the low limit of the first ramp, -10V to 10V; with the low limit above the high one the two are swapped
Sets the high limit of the first ramp, -10V to 10V
Sets the speed of the first ramp, -10 to 10; that figure is volts per second with its delta jack empty, and volts per second per volt when a cable is patched there
Multiplies the speed of the first ramp by 50
Sets the first ramp back to 0V, or to whichever limit is nearer when 0V lies outside the pair
Sets the low limit of the second ramp, -10V to 10V; with the low limit above the high one the two are swapped
Sets the high limit of the second ramp, -10V to 10V
Sets the speed of the second ramp, -10 to 10; that figure is volts per second with its delta jack empty, and volts per second per volt when a cable is patched there
Multiplies the speed of the second ramp by 50
Sets the second ramp back to 0V, or to whichever limit is nearer when 0V lies outside the pair

inputs.text: Sets the speed of the first ramp: volts per second is this voltage times that ramp's speed trimpot, and patching a cable here also starts the ramp moving while its gate jack is empty
Lets the first ramp move while this reads 1V or more and holds it in place below that
Sets the first ramp back to 0V on each rising edge above 1V
Sets the speed of the second ramp: volts per second is this voltage times that ramp's speed trimpot, and patching a cable here also starts the ramp moving while its gate jack is empty
Lets the second ramp move while this reads 1V or more and holds it in place below that
Sets the second ramp back to 0V on each rising edge above 1V

outputs.text: The first ramp's present value in volts, which is also the number printed below it
The second ramp's present value in volts, which is also the number printed below it

notes: a ramp moves only while its gate jack reads 1V or more, or, with that jack empty, while a cable is patched to its delta jack; with both jacks empty it does not move at all
this module passes a memory connection through: it takes the module immediately to its right as its host and adds its own two ramp values as an extra memory channel
the green lamp of a pair lights when that ramp is sitting at its high limit and the red one when it is at its low limit
the whole memory set, the host's channels and this module's two ramps, is offered to an Accessor or DMA-FX placed immediately to the left, which is what lets several be stacked side by side
menu: Wraparound — makes a ramp that reaches one limit carry on from the other instead of stopping, and lights both limit lamps at half brightness to say so
